summary: Sprint 5 successfully resolved all 3 critical orchestrator issues identified by implementation team through automatic feature activation and zero-configuration design

extracted_lessons.content: When implementing orchestrator fixes, ensure all features are automatic (zero configuration) to prevent agent-level complexity and configuration drift. Automatic activation based on context presence minimizes integration risk.

Use Redis for ephemeral context storage (epic/phase/success criteria) with TTL management, enabling dynamic information propagation between orchestrator and CLI-spawned agents without explicit parameter passing.

Maintain cost-efficiency goals during feature additions by validating performance metrics alongside functional requirements. Sprint 5 preserved 97% cost savings while adding epic context, CFN protocol, and heartbeat monitoring.

Design orchestration protocols with backward compatibility using conditional activation based on context presence (e.g., only execute CFN protocol when taskId present). This enables graceful feature introduction without breaking existing workflows.

Avoid manual configuration and hard-coded contexts in agent spawning. Direct Task() spawning worked but required verbose manual context in every prompt. Automatic context injection is more maintainable and reduces errors.
Implement heartbeat monitoring with 30-second intervals to balance false positive prevention with hung agent detection. Too frequent causes overhead, too infrequent causes delayed failure detection.

Prioritize comprehensive test coverage across multiple dimensions (build, Redis ops, integration, functions) with 100% pass rate validation. Sprint 5 achieved 17/17 tests passing, catching issues before production.
